summary: A two-day marine science program for 90 students in Key Largo, organized into three cohorts that rotate through fish identification, a lionfish lesson, kayaking, snorkeling, an ecology hike and a coral nursery visit across REEF, Pennekamp and the MOTE Coral Nursery.

rotation.heading: Three Cohorts, One Coordinated Schedule
rotation.intro: Students are divided into three cohorts, A, B and C, that keep the same letter both days. Cohorts rotate between the REEF campus, Pennekamp Coral Reef State Park and the MOTE Coral Nursery, then come together for meals and an evening program.
notes: Cohorts keep the same letter on both days.
Two buses (Bus 1 and Bus 2) move cohorts between REEF, Pennekamp and the MOTE Coral Nursery; bus times will be confirmed.
Evening program: dinner at 7:00 PM and Human Impact Skits at 8:00 PM, both at the Holiday Inn event space. End times will be confirmed.
Showers follow the water activities at Pennekamp.

days.title: Welcome to the Reef
days.theme: Three cohorts rotate between REEF, Pennekamp and the MOTE Coral Nursery, then come together for dinner and an evening program.

blocks.title: Citizen Science & Fish Identification
blocks.description: Students learn how REEF's volunteer divers and snorkelers identify fish and record what they see, then practice the same identification and survey skills used in REEF's Volunteer Fish Survey Project.

blocks.title: MOTE Coral Nursery
blocks.description: Students visit the MOTE Coral Nursery in Key Largo to see how coral restoration helps reefs recover.

blocks.title: Ecology Hike / Beach Time
blocks.description: A guided ecology hike at Pennekamp, followed by beach time.

blocks.title: Kayaking at Pennekamp (Mangrove Tour)
blocks.description: Students paddle through a mangrove ecosystem with a guide and learn why mangroves matter to the reef.

blocks.title: Snorkel Trip
blocks.description: Students snorkel a Key Largo coral reef and record the fish they find. Showers follow.

blocks.title: Dinner
blocks.description: Dinner at the Holiday Inn event space.

blocks.title: Human Impact Skits
blocks.description: All three cohorts come together for Human Impact Skits at the Holiday Inn event space.

studentsWill: Practice the fish identification and survey skills REEF's citizen scientists use.
Visit a coral nursery and a Key Largo reef.
Explore a mangrove ecosystem by kayak.

days.title: Coral, Fish & Citizen Science
days.theme: Cohorts keep their letters and rotate through the remaining experiences, then share dinner at Pennekamp before departing.

blocks.title: MOTE Coral Nursery
blocks.description: Students visit the MOTE Coral Nursery in Key Largo to see how coral restoration helps reefs recover.

blocks.title: Snorkel Trip
blocks.description: Students snorkel a Key Largo coral reef and record the fish they find. Showers follow.

blocks.title: Ecology Hike / Beach Time
blocks.description: A guided ecology hike at Pennekamp, followed by beach time.

blocks.title: Lionfish Lesson
blocks.description: Students investigate invasive lionfish, looking at their anatomy and adaptations and learning why lionfish are a conservation challenge for Florida Keys reefs.

blocks.title: Kayaking at Pennekamp (Mangrove Tour)
blocks.description: Students paddle through a mangrove ecosystem with a guide and learn why mangroves matter to the reef.

blocks.title: Beach Time & Snorkel Check-In
blocks.description: Beach time at Pennekamp while the cohort checks in for the afternoon snorkel trip.

blocks.title: Showers / Field Time
blocks.description: Showers and field time after the day's activities.

studentsWill: Understand how coral restoration and REEF fish survey data help protect reefs.
Snorkel a Key Largo coral reef and record the fish they find.
